questions.question: What does Salesforce Connect let users do with external data, without ever storing a copy in Salesforce?
options: Automatically migrate it permanently into standard Salesforce objects
View and interact with it as external objects, queried live from the external system
Cache it for 24 hours before refreshing
Encrypt it at rest using Salesforce Shield
questions.explanation: Salesforce Connect maps external rows to external objects and queries the source system live — no local copy, no staleness window.

questions.question: Which adapter would you use to connect Salesforce Connect to a system that exposes an OData 4.0 endpoint?
options: The OData 4.0 adapter
The Cross-Org Adapter
A Custom Adapter built with DataSource.Connection
There is no adapter for OData, it requires Apex
questions.explanation: Salesforce Connect ships standard OData 2.0 and 4.0 adapters for systems that already speak OData — no custom code needed.

questions.question: What's the main trade-off of Salesforce Connect compared to syncing data into native Salesforce objects?
options: Salesforce Connect is always faster than native objects
There is no trade-off, Salesforce Connect is strictly better in every case
Data is always current with no storage cost, but read performance depends on the external system staying fast and available
Salesforce Connect requires copying all the data in nightly
questions.explanation: Live access avoids staleness and storage cost, but adds a runtime dependency on the external system's uptime and speed — every view is a live call.

questions.question: Why check for an existing OData endpoint before building a Custom Adapter?
options: Custom Adapters are deprecated and no longer supported
OData endpoints are required by Salesforce for all external systems
Custom Adapters can only connect to other Salesforce orgs
A Custom Adapter is real engineering work; an existing OData endpoint lets you skip that with a standard adapter
questions.explanation: Confirm the source can't already speak OData (or isn't another Salesforce org, which uses the Cross-Org Adapter) before committing to custom Apex development.

questions.question: When would a traditional batch sync likely be a better choice than Salesforce Connect for a given object?
options: Whenever the data changes more than once a day
Never, Salesforce Connect should always be preferred
Only when the external system is another Salesforce org
When Salesforce needs heavy reporting/automation against the data, or slightly-stale data is acceptable
questions.explanation: Live external objects have real limitations around reporting/automation features and depend on the source system's responsiveness; a sync is often simpler when live access isn't actually needed.
